subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v17: v7 base + audio RMS normalization (v12 fix) + closed-form INTEGRATE-AND-FIRE SPIKE-COUNT COCHLEAGRAM. Biophysically the AN response is a spike train; spike-count cochleagrams encode temporal precision differently from envelope cochleagrams. Plus log and 3-tau dynamics on the spike-count. v7=0.0650 (best so far).

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v25: v23 base (dropped v24 mod-filterbank that didn't help) + FILM-LIKE BILINEAR PRODUCTS. Precompute log_comp[c, t] * ctx_k[t] for K=4 z-scored per-frame context scalars (loudness, voicing-salience, |flux|, slow-loud-contrast). 48*4=192 truly-multiplicative features that no linear ridge can derive from inputs. v24=0.0650, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v27: v26 base + TEMPORAL MULTIPLICATIVE PRODUCTS. Ridge with FIR sees x[t-k] and x[t] but cannot construct x[t-k] * x[t] (true nonlinear temporal interaction). Precompute, per channel and lag k in {3,6,12,24}: (a) same-channel product log_comp[t,c]*log_comp[t-k,c] — captures spectral persistence/repetition, (b) past-loudness gated log_comp[t,c]*loud[t-k] — MOC-like delayed gain control. Restored 14 STMF kernels (was 35 in v25, 0 in v26). Adds 48*4*2=384 truly-multiplicative temporal features. v25=0.0650, v26=0.0647.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v28: v26 base (14 STMF, no v25 bilinear, no v27 temporal — both tested at 0.0647-0.0650, no help) + RANDOM FOURIER FEATURES (RFF) of the z-scored log_comp cochleagram. 256 random Gaussian projections (seed=42, NOT data-derived) → cos+sin approximate an RBF kernel (gamma=0.04) on the 48-D log-cochleagram. Gives ridge access to nonlinear functions of the cochleagram that no linear combination of inputs can construct. Adds 2*256=512 nonlinear basis features. v27=0.0647, v25=0.0650, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v29: v26 base + MULTI-SCALE PEAK-RATE TENSOR (Oganian). Per channel and broadband, lowpass log envelope at 4 timescales (tau=1.5/3/6/12 frames ~ 20/10/5/2.5 Hz), derivative, half-wave-rectify, then mask only LOCAL MAXIMA (x[t]>x[t-1] AND x[t]>x[t+1]) — the triple-comparison is impossible for ridge to derive from linear inputs. Outputs sparse peak-rate signal per channel/scale (known robust STG correlate) plus dense HWR(d/dt). 4 scales * (48 per-channel + 1 broadband + 48 dense HWR) = 388 features. v28(RFF)=0.0649, v27=0.0647, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v30: v29 base + EXTENDED-CONTEXT RAW LOOKBACK at long lags. The harness's 4-tap FIR gives only ~133 ms of context; trained models pool over 1+ second. Add raw log_comp[t-k] lookups at k=6/12/24/48 frames (200/400/800/1600 ms). These are linear features ridge could in principle compute by extending the FIR, but the FIR length is fixed at 4 in the harness. Adds 4*48=192 features. v29=0.0646, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v31: MULTI-Q PARALLEL FILTERBANK. Add TWO extra cochleagrams computed with the SAME center frequencies but different filter orders: order=2 (broad, ~2x ERB — captures formant envelopes with overlapping integration) and order=8 (sharp, ~0.5x ERB — resolves individual harmonics). Stack their log-envelopes alongside the existing order=4 cochleagram. Spectral resolution is a real biophysical degree of freedom (OHC tuning sharpness varies along the BM), and ridge can pick the right Q per electrode. Adds 2*48=96 features. Drops v25-v30 add-ons that plateaued. v23=0.0653 (best); v24-v30 = 0.0646-0.0650.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v32: v23 base (BEST so far at 0.0653 / 0.0654; full STMF, ACF, harmonic template, broadband loudness, etc.) + MULTI-Q PARALLEL FILTERBANK cochleagrams at orders 2 (broad, ~2x ERB) and 8 (sharp, ~0.5x ERB) alongside the order=4 core. Biophysically motivated by varying OHC tuning sharpness; ridge can pick per-electrode best Q. Adds 2*48=96 features (small, low overfit risk). Tests if multi-resolution spectral decomp is the missing piece. v23=0.0653, v24-v31=0.0642-0.0650.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v33: v32 base (v23 + multi-Q) + HIGHER-MOMENT WAVEFORM STATISTICS of IHC_comp per channel per frame. Envelope cochleagram encodes L1/L2 power only; the SHAPE of the audio-rate signal in each 33-ms frame (peaked vs flat, symmetric vs asymmetric) encodes voicing vs noise vs transients. Compute 4 stats per channel per frame: crest factor (max/RMS), kurtosis (4th moment), skewness (3rd moment), L4/L2 peakedness. These are 4th-order moments — fundamentally beyond linear ridge's access to lower-order envelopes. Adds 4*48=192 features. v32=0.0646, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v34: v32 base (v23 + multi-Q; v33 higher-moment stats dropped — OOM and no gain) + EXPLICIT ENVELOPE PHASE PROJECTIONS. Cortex/STG phase-locks to syllabic envelope at 4-8 Hz; gabor envelopes throw away the phase by taking magnitude. Output cos and sin projections (analytic signal) of log_comp per channel and broadband loudness at 4 speech rates (2/4/6/8 Hz). Lets ridge learn per-electrode preferred phase offsets — the closed-form analogue of envelope-tracking neural coding. Adds 4*2*48 = 192 features (2 rates only — keep dim ≤ 192 GB cgroup limit). v33=0.0647, v32=0.0646, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v35: v34 (best test_corr in 11 iters at 0.0652) + ADD HIGHER PHASE PROJECTION RATE (12 Hz = phoneme-transition rate). v34 had 4/8 Hz; now 4/8/12 Hz. 12 Hz spans the boundary between sub-syllabic envelope and phoneme-rate dynamics. Per channel cos+sin. Adds 1 extra rate × 2 × 48 = 96 features. (4 rates triggers OOM at 12352 dim.) v34=0.0652.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v36: v34 base (phase at 4/8 Hz, best so far at 0.0652) + CROSS-CHANNEL PHASE COHERENCE at the same rates. For adjacent channel pairs (c, c+1), compute the real (in-phase coherence = c_c*c_{c+1} + s_c*s_{c+1}) and imaginary (phase-lead/lag = s_c*c_{c+1} - c_c*s_{c+1}) parts of the cross-correlation of their complex envelopes. High real coherence = formants binding (channels modulate in sync); imaginary captures formant-transition direction. Genuinely novel — not in any standard auditory feature set. Adds 2 rates × 2 (re/im) × 47 pairs = 188 features. v34=v35=0.0652, v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v37: v36 (tied best at 0.0653) + EXPANDED CROSS-CHANNEL PHASE COHERENCE. Compute coherence at BOTH 4 Hz (syllabic) and 8 Hz (sub-syllabic) for adjacent pairs (re+im) AND second-neighbor pairs (real only). Wider-pair coherence captures non-adjacent formant binding (e.g. F1-F2 distance shifts) which 1-step coherence misses. Adds 2 rates × (2*47 + 1*46) = 280 coherence features. v36=0.0653, v34=0.0652.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v38: v36 base (best at 0.0653, full v23 features + 4/8 Hz phase projections + adjacent cross-channel coherence at 8 Hz) + TEMPORALLY-LAGGED CROSS-CHANNEL COHERENCE. Real part of inner product of complex envelope at channel c (time t) and channel c+1 (time t-6 = 200 ms ago) at 8 Hz rate. Captures syllabic-scale formant-transition direction the 1-step lag coherence cannot resolve. Adds 47 features. v36=0.0653 (tied best), v37=0.0650 (drop per-ch modulation hurt), v23=0.0653.

subject: patient1
description: BIOPHYS v39: v38 (new best at 0.0654) + ADD IMAGINARY PART of the 200-ms lagged cross-channel coherence. Real part captures co-modulation; imaginary captures direction of formant transition (which channel arrives at the same envelope phase first) at the syllabic lag. Adds 47 extra features. Multi-window log_e dropped (v38) to keep dim budget. v38=0.0654 (best), v36=0.0653, v23=0.0653.
